question: The SI unit of 'ultimate stress' is ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __pascal (Pa)**(Pa)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ultimate stress__ is the maximum stress that a material can withstand before failure.
 
• It is measured in pascal (Pa), which is the SI unit of pressure or stress.
 
• The formula for stress is stress = force / area.
 
• 1 Pascal is equivalent to 1 Newton per square meter (N/m²).
 
• Materials with higher ultimate stress are considered stronger and more resistant to deformation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Stress Types:**
 
 
• Stress can be classified as tensile stress, compressive stress, and shear stress.
 
• Tensile stress occurs when a material is being stretched.
 
• Compressive stress occurs when a material is being compressed.
 
• Shear stress occurs when a material is being acted upon by opposing forces.
 
 
 
• **Units of Stress:**
 
 
• Stress is commonly measured in units such as pascal (Pa), bar, or psi (pounds per square inch).
 
• 1 bar = 100,000 pascals.
 
• 1 psi = 6894.76 pascals.
